title: Invoices with the owner at the time
prompt: Sales pays commission to whoever owned the account when an invoice was raised, not to today's owner. Write `owner_report(invoices, history)` so each invoice gets the account's owner and segment from the type 2 history.
rules: Use the account version that was valid at the start (midnight) of `invoice_date`: `effective_from` at or before it, and `effective_to` NULL or after it.
The history starts on 1 January 2026, so report only invoices dated from then on.
Every such invoice is in the report once. If no version of its account was valid that day, `account_owner` and `segment` are NULL.
hints: This is a join on the account and on a time range. Give both sides an alias and put the whole condition in `join(..., on=condition, ...)`.
`F.col("i.invoice_date").cast("timestamp")` is midnight of that day, so it compares with the history's timestamps.
Which join keeps an invoice that finds no version?
starter:
import shutil

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from delta.tables import DeltaTable

PATH = "/tmp/crm/dim_accounts"
COLS = ["account_id", "account_name", "industry", "country", "segment", "account_owner", "credit_limit", "created_on", "is_active"]


def build_history(accounts, customer_cdc):
    # The type 2 history: the 1 January snapshot, then the change feed applied as one batch. Don't change this.
    shutil.rmtree(PATH, ignore_errors=True)  # start from an empty folder on every run
    (accounts
        .withColumn("effective_from", F.lit("2026-01-01 00:00:00").cast("timestamp"))
        .withColumn("effective_to", F.lit(None).cast("timestamp"))
        .withColumn("is_current", F.lit(True))
        .write.format("delta").save(PATH))
    newest_first = Window.partitionBy("account_id").orderBy(F.col("sequence").desc())
    latest = customer_cdc.withColumn("rn", F.row_number().over(newest_first)).filter(F.col("rn") == 1).drop("rn")
    (DeltaTable.forPath(spark, PATH).alias("t")
        .merge(latest.alias("s"), "t.account_id = s.account_id AND t.is_current")
        .whenMatchedUpdate(set={"effective_to": "s.changed_at", "is_current": "false"})
        .execute())
    (latest.filter(F.col("op") != "D")
        .select(*COLS, F.col("changed_at").alias("effective_from"),
                F.lit(None).cast("timestamp").alias("effective_to"), F.lit(True).alias("is_current"))
        .write.format("delta").mode("append").save(PATH))


def owner_report(invoices, history):
    # Each invoice from 1 January 2026, with the account's owner and segment on the invoice date.
    pass

def solve(accounts, customer_cdc, invoices):
    build_history(accounts, customer_cdc)
    history = spark.read.format("delta").load(PATH)
    return owner_report(invoices, history)
explanation: Join the 2026 invoices to the history on the account and on validity: `(F.col("h.effective_from") <= day) & (F.col("h.effective_to").isNull() | (day < F.col("h.effective_to")))`, with `day` the invoice date as a timestamp. Versions don't overlap, so each invoice matches at most one, and a left join keeps the invoices that match none, such as one raised after its account was deleted. Joining on `account_id` alone gives one row per version, and joining only the current versions credits today's owner: ACC-0001's 5 February invoice belongs to Dana Whitlock, who owned it until 10 March.
